correctness.rationale: For arbitrary invariant μ, P_n X_n and X_0 have identical laws; along any bounded-subsequence products, c0 yields almost-sure convergence to zero and therefore μ=δ_0. No integration or independence is used. The fixed-point vector and Bernoulli coding are verified exactly for all indices; continuity/compactness and strong mixing follow by uniform tail control and cylinder independence plus monotone-class extension. The proof covers real and complex weights, including lack of a lower weight bound.

value.rationale: The theorem answers the precise c0 existence characterization explicitly posed as Question 7.7 in the 2023 Grivaux–Matheron–Menet work, beyond their product-law and ℓp results. It sharpens the hypercyclicity-versus-mixing distinction by showing some hypercyclic c0 shifts have no invariant probability except δ_0, and supplies compact nonatomic mixing examples exactly at the divergence threshold.
